title: Find the Median of the Uniqueness Array
summary: Given an integer array nums, compute the sorted array of distinct elements for all subarrays.
statement: Given an integer array nums, compute the sorted array of distinct elements for all subarrays. The task is to find the median of this sorted array of distinct elements. The median is the middle element of the sorted array; if the array has an even number of elements, the median is the smaller of the two middle elements.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array.
The uniqueness array contains the number of distinct values in every nonempty contiguous subarray.
Sort those counts and return the lower median, using the smaller middle value when their number is even.
hints: For a candidate d, the number of subarrays with at most d distinct values is monotone in d.
Binary-search the first d whose at-most count reaches the lower-median rank; compute counts by sliding window.
Shrink while distinct>d and add window length at every right endpoint; compare the total with ceil(subarrayCount/2).
The at-most count is the sorted uniqueness-array prefix length, so its first value reaching the target rank is exactly that order statistic.
editorial: The at-most count is the sorted uniqueness-array prefix length, so its first value reaching the target rank is exactly that order statistic.

tests.explanation: The uniqueness counts are 1,1,1,2,2,3; the lower median is one.
Counts 1,1,1,1,2,2 sort to the same order, whose lower median is one.
